claims.text: Coupled tribo-corrosion degradation in HEAs is governed by the synergy between mechanically induced passive-film disruption and rapid repassivation.
The multi-element composition of HEAs enables rapid repassivation.
Multiple elements capable of forming protective oxides enhance repassivation efficiency.
The rate and extent of total degradation are determined by the balance between passive-film breakdown during wear and repassivation efficiency.
The initial HEA has a homogeneous, stable passive oxide film formed under ambient conditions.
Passive-film composition and integrity are influenced by the alloy's multi-element content.
Mechanical sliding disrupts the passive film and exposes fresh alloy surface to the electrolyte.
The exposed HEA surface can rapidly form new protective oxides.
Repeated passive-film disruption can outpace repassivation and thereby produce synergistic degradation.
Repassivation efficiency depends on alloy composition and the nature of the oxides formed.
Total material loss under tribo-corrosion will exceed the sum of wear-only and corrosion-only losses.
HEAs containing elements that promote rapid and robust repassivation will exhibit a lower magnitude of tribo-corrosion synergy.
Cr, Al, and Ti are examples of elements that promote rapid and robust repassivation in HEAs.
Both wear and corrosion components will increase under coupled tribo-corrosion relative to their respective isolated baselines.
Greater HEA repassivation ability will mitigate the increases in both wear and corrosion components.
The prediction applies to HEAs containing sufficient concentrations of repassivating elements when environmental conditions permit passive-film formation.
The prediction may fail for HEAs lacking repassivating elements.
High sliding speeds or loads can prevent effective repassivation and cause the prediction to fail.
Electrolytes that inhibit oxide formation can cause the prediction to fail.
HEAs should exhibit enhanced repassivation and reduced tribo-corrosion synergy relative to conventional alloys tested under identical conditions.
